children: By George Glover and Kit Norton
Stocks fell on Tuesday after the consumer price index for October showed hotter-than-expected inflation and raised the odds of an interest-rate hike from the Federal Reserve on Dec. 9.

Artificial-intelligence start-up Anthropic, however, is pushing ahead with its trillion-dollar initial public offering. Anthropic said in a filing Tuesday that it and some of its investors would sell 825 million Class A shares at an estimated IPO price of between $70 and $78 a share. At the top of that range, Anthropic would raise about $64.4 billion from the offering.

Nvidia dropped 3.1%. The Federal Bureau of Investigation is looking into CEO Jensen Huang's romantic relationship with a suspected Chinese spy, according to President Donald Trump. That hasn't stopped some investors, including ARK's Cathie Wood, from buying the dip.
Advanced Micro Devices and Broadcom, on the flipside, rose 5.6% and 4.4%, respectively.

CoreWeave gained 3%. The AI cloud computing company reports quarterly earnings after the closing bell Tuesday. Depending on what CoreWeave has to say, the massive funding for the AI buildout and the potential for debt could rock the stock market once more.

Take-Two Interactive rose 5% and was one of the best-performing stocks in the S&P 500 for the trading session. The videogame publisher's second-quarter bookings came in just below Wall Street's estimates — but that doesn't matter, with Grand Theft Auto VI about to launch. "It's just uncharted territory with preorders trending well above our expectations," CEO Strauss Zelnick told Barron's.

Skydance dropped 8.7% and was the worst performing component in the S&P 500. The company warned in its third-quarter earnings report that poor performance from the Warner Bros. film slate in the fourth quarter could impact profits by up to $200 million compared with prior expectations. The company didn't offer complete fourth-quarter guidance, opting instead to issue full-year outlooks moving forward.
Hims & Hers Health fell 10%. The telehealth company posted a surprise third-quarter loss and narrowed its full-year sales outlook as it struggles to deal with higher costs.
Lucid rose 13% even as the luxury electric-car maker missed analysts' third-quarter earnings and revenue targets and said it had expanded its loan from Saudi Arabia's sovereign wealth fund.
Digital Turbine sank 35% to $7.40 after the company's plans to invest in data and AI to support longer-term growth sucked all the air out of stronger-than-expected quarterly earnings.
On Holdings rattled investors with third-quarter earnings showing a sales slowdown in the Americas region and a lower-than-expected direct-to-consumer segment. The stock declined 7.4%.
AAON surged 22% as booming demand for data-center cooling equipment propelled the company's quarterly earnings and led AAON to raise its annual outlook.
